analysis_plan: Use the fresh source-checkpoint test run as the accuracy baseline.
For each cohort-B assignment seed, subtract transferred test accuracy from source test accuracy and report the mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum loss in percentage points.
Report transferred teacher agreement and KL alongside accuracy, and inspect quad-window empty fractions and span statistics before interpreting the loss.
Treat assignment seeds as device-allocation sensitivity for one fixed trained model, not as independent model-training seeds.

arms.description: Fresh held-out test evaluation of the selected cohort-A four-device checkpoint.
Zero-update reprojection of the selected four-device checkpoint onto five deterministic cohort-B device assignments.
Fresh held-out test evaluation of each transferred cohort-B checkpoint.

completion_criteria: The source checkpoint has one fresh completed 10,000-example test evaluation.
All five cohort-B assignment seeds complete a zero-learning-rate deployment with exactly one batch and no conductance update.
All five transferred checkpoints have one fresh completed 10,000-example test evaluation.
Every run retains the source checkpoint, teacher checkpoint, device-data, config, and study provenance in its native manifest.
The final interpretation reports accuracy loss distribution as exploratory single-model evidence.
hypothesis: Reprojecting the selected cohort-A four-device quad-common-window checkpoint onto held-out cohort-B devices will reduce mean held-out test accuracy by more than 1 percentage point after scalar recalibration alone.
motivation: Quantify the immediate hardware-transfer penalty for the four-device initialization and exercise the new result workflow on a small matched multi-run study.
title: Four-device cohort-A to cohort-B transfer across five assignments
